title: Capacity slotting and staggered upgrade simulator for Dedicated fleets
creator: Miles Chen
description:
Problem: Upgrades, node drains and maintenance windows on Dedicated fleets can cause transient throughput and tail-latency regressions. We need a lightweight simulator and capacity-slotting strategy to validate staggered upgrade policies, slot sizes, and KV-cache prewarm heuristics before rolling to production.

Goal: Build a deterministic simulation harness that models slot allocation, staggered upgrade waves, autoscaler behavior, and per-application throughput contracts. Use the simulator to produce SLO risk curves (probability of p99 > target, throughput loss %) given different slotting and prewarm configurations. Deliver a recommended staging policy and a gating checklist for safe fleet upgrades.
acceptance_criteria: Simulator runs a 24h synthetic workload and outputs: per-slot token/sec, p50/p95/p99 latency, and percent of requests dropped or backpressured
Produce a default set of upgrade profiles (fast, balanced, cautious) with recommended slot sizes and stagger windows
Validate that recommended 'balanced' profile keeps p99 <= 250ms and throughput loss < 3% for 95% of simulated runs under historical traffic mix
Generate a short playbook (5 steps) that ops can follow for a staged Dedicated fleet upgrade using the selected profile
Add artifacts: GitHub repo with harness, Confluence design doc, and a dashboard template showing simulator outputs mapped to SLO risk
notes: 2026-03-05 - Ticket created by Miles Chen. Initial ask from Customer Success: Dedicated customer reported 12% token/sec dip during last rolling upgrade; need an offline tool to reason about trade-offs.
2026-03-06 - Design sync with Platform SRE (Diego Martinez) and Runtime (Priya Nair): agreed on modeling KV cache warmup, request routing failover, and autoscaler latency to scale-up events.

2026-03-08 - Prototype: local harness can simulate N hosts, slot size, and stagger windows. Early results show small slots (<2%) reduce peak impact but increase orchestration time. Trade-off: smaller slots lower SLO risk at cost of upgrade duration.

2026-03-09 - Decision: include an 'aggression' knob that controls whether autoscaler will temporarily overprovision during maintenance waves and a 'preheat' parameter for KV cache hit-rate restoration.

2026-03-10 - Engineering review (Hannah Lee): prefer deterministic seed for Monte Carlo runs, add support for tenant-weighted workloads (some customers produce long-tail sequences), and model regional capacity constraints.
2026-03-11 - UX/Operations input (Samira Bello): request generated playbook steps be machine-readable (yaml checklist) to allow automation in maintenance-runbooks repo.

2026-03-12 - Integration plan: create repo github.com/redwood-inference/dedicated-upgrade-sim, PR skeleton created: PR#642 (link below). Next: add historical traffic traces and run 500 Monte Carlo variants to tune balanced profile.
risks_and_open_questions: How accurately can we model KV-cache warmup time for mixed quantized model pools? (need input from Runtime team)
Autoscaler behavior is currently modeled as step-based; investigate modeling gradual CPU/GPU allocation delays seen in cloud providers
Potential mismatch between synthetic workload and production request skew; plan to replay sampled traces from prod for validation
Operational buy-in: will Sales/Support accept a recommended 10h upgrade window for very large fleets? Need stakeholder signoff
plan: Week 1: flesh out simulator core (slot allocator, wave scheduler, autoscaler stub, KV warmup model)
Week 2: ingest sampled production traces, add tenant-weighted traffic and Monte Carlo runner, run baseline experiments
Week 3: define profiles (fast/balanced/cautious), generate SLO risk reports, iterate on knob defaults with SRE
Week 4: ship repo, Confluence doc, and ops playbook; run a pilot upgrade on a non-critical dedicated fleet with observability dashboard
recent_progress: 2026-03-09 - Prototype harness bench: 10k host-step simulation executes in ~18s locally (deterministic seed).
2026-03-10 - Added tenant-weight weighting and per-tenant sequence length distribution. First run indicates long-tail tenants disproportionately affect p99 during upgrades.
2026-03-12 - PR#642 created with simulator scaffold and basic reports (CSV + Grafana JSON). Requesting runtime review from Priya Nair and SRE review from Diego Martinez.
suggested_next_actions: Review PR#642 and provide runtime model parameters (KV warmup half-life, cache hit-rate ramp) by 2026-03-15
Ops to nominate a pilot Dedicated fleet for a dry-run by 2026-03-22
Schedule a cross-team demo of simulator outputs and proposed profiles with PM and SRE on 2026-03-18
